headline: High-risk data and capability overlap: shared writes, shared mutable resources, and unverified cross-agent handoff create dangerous default failure modes.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Copilot reads repo context and open buffers, while semantica can ingest local files, web pages, and MCP resources. There is no direct shared channel documented, but semantica’s MCP/file ingestion could carry Copilot-authored content into a parser that may treat it as trusted. The pathway exists in default tooling, though not via a proven bridge.
conditions: IF semantica ingests Copilot-generated text from files or MCP resources without provenance checks, injection risk materializes.
IF Copilot Workspace edits are copied into semantica inputs, attacker-controlled instructions can traverse the pair.
mitigations: Disable automatic ingestion of Copilot-generated artifacts into semantica inputs.
Add provenance tags to files passed between agents.
Review any semantica MCP resource before parsing.
Use a separate staging directory for handoffs.
requires-engineering: enforce content-type and provenance filtering at the bridge.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Copilot touches source code and open editor buffers, and semantica handles enterprise data, contracts, secrets, and audit trails. Both can read/write files, and semantica also handles tokens, passwords, and private keys. A shared workspace or copied buffers would expose sensitive data to a second agent that can transmit via allowlisted network or APIs, so the blast radius is broad.
conditions: IF both agents access the same repository or workspace, sensitive files can flow from Copilot to semantica.
IF semantica is pointed at directories containing secrets or contracts, its API/network surfaces can propagate that data outward.
mitigations: Separate code and enterprise-data workspaces.
Remove secrets from any shared directory before running semantica.
Restrict semantica to a read-only subset of files.
Rotate any credentials present in shared buffers.
requires-engineering: add per-agent data-loss-prevention and workspace isolation.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents can write the filesystem and modify git state. Copilot’s Workspace plans apply edits for human review, while semantica can also modify git and operate over shared context graphs. In a shared repo, concurrent writes or git mutations can overwrite each other or corrupt state; no locking mechanism is documented in either profile.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same git checkout, conflicting edits can be committed or overwritten.
IF semantica and Copilot run concurrently without external locking, file and git state divergence is likely.
mitigations: Assign each agent a separate checkout.
Pause one agent before the other writes.
Use git worktrees for parallel tasks.
Review and merge diffs manually before commit.
requires-engineering: add file-level and git-level locking.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Copilot produces edits and chat output that semantica can ingest through files, web pages, APIs, or MCP resources. Semantica’s deterministic graph/provenance tooling may still treat imported content as authoritative unless explicitly verified. That creates a default cascade where one agent’s output becomes the other’s input and downstream actions can amplify a mistaken suggestion.
conditions: IF Copilot-generated text is imported into semantica without verification, errors can propagate into graphs or decision records.
IF semantica uses imported content to drive downstream actions, a mistaken Copilot suggestion can cascade.
mitigations: Require human verification before semantica ingests Copilot output.
Mark Copilot output as untrusted in semantica provenance.
Limit semantica to summarization, not action-taking, for Copilot-derived inputs.
Compare imported facts against source documents.
requires-engineering: add provenance-aware trust scoring between agents.

E_compliance.rationale: Copilot is a closed-source vendor service with GitHub/Microsoft network egress, while semantica is self-hosted and handles enterprise data, contracts, and secrets. If regulated or confidential data from semantica flows into Copilot’s vendor backend, residency and retention obligations can be violated. The profiles do not show a DPA or residency control, so uncertainty pushes this to high.
conditions: IF semantica data includes regulated records and is sent to Copilot, vendor-side processing may breach policy.
IF the deployment requires data residency controls and Copilot is used on that data, compliance gaps appear.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of Copilot prompts.
Use semantica only on approved local datasets.
Document a data-classification rule for cross-agent handoff.
Review vendor retention settings for Copilot.
requires-engineering: add residency and retention enforcement at the orchestrator.
